doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Woody Herman, Chubby Jackson and Europe
title: Woody Herman as leader of the greatest band
summary: Gibbs admires how Woody put up with so much; the band played month-long club engagements and lost money.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It must have been hard for Woody to deal with that.

I admire him so much because he put up with so much. And the reason he put up with it, that was the greatest band in the world at that time. The greatest band. It was so great that instead of playing one night stands and barns or ballroom or whatever, where you make your money, we stayed at the Royal Roost in New York for a month, in California at the Empire Room for a month, Chicago at the Blue Note for a month, and you can’t make any money in night clubs. No way can you pay a sixteen, seventeen piece band and come out. No way can you do it. And so he’d lose money all the time. But he was so proud of that band. Really proud. Because it was the greatest band in the world. Every one of those guys in that band, the Four Brothers Band, went on to become big jazz stars or movie picture writers, arrangers.
